message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`; no internet), the repo layout, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: `lini desugar FILE` — "print a file lowered to primitives + .lini-* classes" — byte-identical to the original (`executable desugar FILE`). `src/desugar.rs` has the stub `pub fn desugar(src: &str) -> Result<String, Diag>`; main.rs prints its result and handles errors/stdin/missing files (verify those wrappers too: errors print `file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1).

Output shape (see `executable desugar assets/test_samples/desugar.lini`, and the outputs for every asset file): a stylesheet block `{ … }` with the root scene config (`layout: flow; padding: 20; gap: 36; font-size: 15;` defaults merged with the user's root declarations), one `.lini-TYPE { … }` rule per type used (defaults merged with the user's `|type| { }` rules, in a fixed registry order; long rules wrap onto an indented line), user classes/vars/bindings as they appear (check), then the canvas: every node as `|primitive#id| .lini-a.lini-b.style-classes { inline decls; } [ children ]`, labels lowered to text children, group labels to `|block| .lini-caption.lini-block [ "…" ]`, auto-created link endpoints declared as `|block#a| .lini-box.lini-block [ "a" ]` at specific positions, links printed with their label lowered into `{ along: 0.33, 0.67; … } [ "lbl" "x" ]`, define bodies materialised per instance, etc. Families lower in rich ways that desugar shows verbatim: tables → cells/header classes, entity, page → frame/ticks/zones/marks + title-block fields, mindmap → topics with `.lini-hue-*`/`.lini-level-N` classes and generated branch links, holes → centerline chrome children, drawings → `px-per-unit`, schematics → parts/pins/labels, sequence, charts, floorplans… The compile pipeline of this repo does NOT implement most of these yet (other agents are working on them in parallel), so implement the lowering *for desugar purposes* inside your own module(s) (src/desugar.rs, src/desugar/*.rs), using the parser's AST (src/ast.rs, src/parser.rs) and the type registry (src/types.rs — note desugar reveals the full default rule text of each type; extend types.rs entries if you find missing/incorrect defaults, that helps everyone, but keep edits additive). Formatting details matter: indentation, line wrapping of long declaration lists (find the width rule), number formatting, string escaping, ordering of rules and declarations, blank lines.

Test corpus: all files under /workspace/assets (test_doc_examples/*.lini, test_doc_examples/blocks/*.lini, test_samples/*.lini) via `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-desugar/executable -a desugar <files>`, plus many synthetic snippets in /tmp/<you>/. Prioritise: core constructs (boxes, groups, captions, badges, rows/columns/grids, text, classes, defines with bodies, links, auto endpoints, user rules) first, then tables/entity, page/title-block, mindmap/tree, then the rest.

Before committing, also run the compile comparison (`cmpw.py /tmp/bin-desugar/executable assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini assets/test_samples/*.lini`, starting count 71/209) to make sure you didn't regress compile if you touched shared files. Commit on your branch and report the desugar pass rate, shared-file edits, and gaps.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

timeout.description: Optional timeout in milliseconds (max 600000 for a foreground command)

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).
- `subcommands`: fmt (src/format*), highlight (src/highlight.rs) are DONE and verified — don't touch.

## Working rules
- Put your feature in its own module(s); keep edits to shared files (main.rs, layout.rs,
  render.rs, compile.rs, scene.rs, types.rs) minimal and additive — other people are editing
  them in parallel and we merge branches afterwards.
- Commit your work on your branch in your worktree (`git add -A && git commit -m ...`) when
  done, and report: what passes, what doesn't, and any shared-file changes you made.

ARCH.md

- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

- `replace_all: true` replaces every occurrence instead.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# usage: cmpw.py BIN [-a "extra args"] [-s N] files...
# Runs the original (/workspace/executable) and BIN on each file (cwd = file's dir),
# compares stdout, stderr and exit code. BIN must be named 'executable' (help text uses argv[0]).
import subprocess,sys,os
mine=sys.argv[1]; args=[]; files=[]; show=0
i=2
while i<len(sys.argv):
    a=sys.argv[i]
    if a=='-a': args=sys.argv[i+1].split(); i+=2; continue
    if a=='-s': show=int(sys.argv[i+1]); i+=2; continue
    files.append(a); i+=1
ORIG='/workspace/executable'
ok=0; bad=[]
for f in files:
    d=os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(f)); b=os.path.basename(f)
    r1=subprocess.run([ORIG]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    try: r2=subprocess.run([mine]+args+[b],capture_output=True,cwd=d,timeout=30)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired: bad.append((f,'TIMEOUT')); continue
    if r1.stdout==r2.stdout and r1.stderr==r2.stderr and r1.returncode==r2.returncode: ok+=1
    else:
        why=[]
        if r1.returncode!=r2.returncode: why.append('exit %d/%d'%(r1.returncode,r2.returncode))
        if r1.stdout!=r2.stdout: why.append('stdout')
        if r1.stderr!=r2.stderr: why.append('stderr')
        bad.append((f,' '.join(why)))
print('OK %d / %d'%(ok,len(files)))
for f,w in (bad[:show] if show else bad): print('  FAIL',f,w)
#!/bin/bash
# usage: dw BIN file.lini [extra args]  -> diff of original vs BIN output (stderr, then stdout)
mine="$1"; f="$2"; shift 2
dir=$(dirname "$f"); b=$(basename "$f")
cd "$dir"
/workspace/executable "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_o.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_oe.$$; e1=$?
"$mine" "$@" "$b" > /tmp/dw_m.$$ 2>/tmp/dw_me.$$; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"
diff /tmp/dw_oe.$$ /tmp/dw_me.$$ | head -10
diff /tmp/dw_o.$$ /tmp/dw_m.$$ | head -${DL:-60}
rm -f /tmp/dw_*.$$
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rr 'lini source' [extra args] -> runs the ORIGINAL on the snippet (file r_in.lini in a private tmp dir)
src="$1"; shift
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rr.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d && /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini; echo "[exit $?]"; rm -rf $d
#!/bin/bash
# usage: rm2 BIN 'lini source' [extra args] -> diff original vs BIN on a snippet
mine="$1"; src="$2"; shift 2
d=$(mktemp -d /tmp/rm2.XXXXXX); printf '%s' "$src" > $d/r_in.lini
cd $d; /workspace/executable "$@" r_in.lini > o1 2>&1; e1=$?; "$mine" "$@" r_in.lini > o2 2>&1; e2=$?
echo "exit $e1 / $e2"; diff o1 o2 | head -${DL:-60}; rm -rf $d

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE). assets/test_doc_examples: blocks prop_activation.lini prop_align.lini prop_along.lini // Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

// Registry order is the order type rules are emitted in the stylesheet.
pub static TYPES: &[TypeDef] = &[
    t!("block", Block, None, "fill: none; stroke: none; stroke-width: 2; padding: 0; gap: 36;"),
    t!("oval", Oval, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; direction: column; gap: 12;"),
    t!("hex", Hex, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; direction: column; gap: 12;"),
    t!("slant", Slant, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; direction: column; gap: 12; skew: 15;"),
    t!("cyl", Cyl, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; direction: column; gap: 12;"),
    t!("diamond", Diamond, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; direction: column; gap: 12;"),
    t!("poly", Poly, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2;"),
    t!("path", Path, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2;"),
    t!("sketch", Sketch, None, "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke-dark; stroke-width: 2;"),
    t!("line", Line, None, "fill: none; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2;"),
    t!("text", Text, None, ""),
    t!("icon", Icon, None, "fill: --icon-fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; width: 32; height: 32;"),
    t!("image", Image, None, ""),
    // templates
    t!("box", Block, Some("block"), "fill: --fill; stroke: --stroke; stroke-width: 2; padding: 20; radius: 8; direction: column; gap: 12;"),
    t!("rect", Block, Some("box"), "radius: 0;"),
    t!("group", Block, Some("block"), "stroke: --group-stroke; stroke-style: dashed; stroke-width: 1; fill: --group-fill; radius: 8; padding: 20;"),
    t!("row", Block, Some("block"), "direction: row;"),
    t!("column", Block, Some("block"), "direction: column;"),
    t!("grid", Block, Some("block"), "layout: grid;"),
    t!("caption", Block, Some("block"), "pin: top left; translate: 0 -20; color: --caption-color; font-scale: 12 15; font-weight: --caption-font-weight;"),

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

// Built-in type registry: every template lowers onto a primitive, with a
// chain of `.lini-*` classes whose defaults cascade base-first.

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub enum Prim {
    Block,
    Oval,
    Hex,
    Slant,
    Cyl,
    Diamond,
    Poly,
    Path,
    Sketch,
    Line,
    Icon,
    Image,
    Text,
}

impl Prim {
    pub fn name(self) -> &'static str {
        match self {
            Prim::Block => "block",
            Prim::Oval => "oval",
            Prim::Hex => "hex",
            Prim::Slant => "slant",
            Prim::Cyl => "cyl",
            Prim::Diamond => "diamond",
            Prim::Poly => "poly",
            Prim::Path => "path",
            Prim::Sketch => "sketch",
            Prim::Line => "line",
            Prim::Icon => "icon",
            Prim::Image => "image",
            Prim::Text => "text",
        }
    }
}

pub struct TypeDef {
    pub name: &'static str,
    pub prim: Prim,
    pub base: Option<&'static str>,
    pub defaults: &'static str,
}

macro_rules! t {
    ($n:expr, $p:ident, $b:expr, $d:expr) => {
        TypeDef { name: $n, prim: Prim::$p, base: $b, defaults: $d }
    };
}

        m = re.match(r'^  (\.lini-[\w-]+) \{$', l)
        if m:

            while sheet[i] != '  }':

            rules[m.group(1)][' '.join(body)] += 1; names.append(m.group(1)); i += 1; continue

    for a, b in zip(names, names[1:]):
        order_pairs[(a, b)] += 1
for k in sorted(rules):

// The order `lini desugar` writes the `.lini-*` rules in, and the default
// rule text of the internal classes the lowering introduces. Types read their
// defaults (and chains) from `types.rs`.

// built-in types and chrome classes, before the user's defines
pub static BUILTIN_ORDER: &[&str] = &[
    "block", "oval", "hex", "slant", "cyl", "diamond", "poly", "path", "line", "icon", "image", "sketch", "box", "rect",
    "group", "caption", "footnote", "badge", "row", "column", "grid", "table", "cell", "header", "footer", "entity",
    "sign", "chart", "pie", "area", "bars", "dots", "bubble", "slice", "axis", "band", "mark", "sequence", "loop", "opt",
    "alt", "else", "note", "balloon", "topic", "mindmap", "drawing", "hole", "centerline", "breakline", "threadline",
    "pitch-circle", "hidden", "shoulder", "surface-finish", "feature-control", "control", "datum", "plane",
    "magnifier", "page", "title-block", "field", "frame", "zone", "tick", "stack", "floorplan", "wall", "partition",
    "door", "door-leaf", "door-swing", "window", "window-sill", "bed", "sofa", "dining", "bath", "appliance",
    "stairs", "stair-tread", "stair-arrow", "schematic", "component", "pin", "pin-stub", "pin-number", "space",
    "label", "junction", "J", "opamp", "gnd", "nc", "R", "C", "L", "D", "LED", "Q", "Y", "F", "FB", "SW", "BT", "V", "I",
    "M", "BZ", "TP",
];

// utility classes the lowering adds, after the user's defines
pub static UTILITY_ORDER: &[&str] = &[
    "align-start",
    "align-end",
    "justify-start",
    "justify-end",
    "sch-line",
    "sch-solid",
    "sch-tag-line",
    "ref",
    "part-value",
    "net-run",
    "net-run-turned",
    "tag-outline",
    "tag-round",
    "tag-flag-left",
    "tag-flag-right",
    "tag-flag-both",
    "sheet-caption",
];

// default rule text of classes that are not types
pub fn class_defaults(name: &str) -> Option<&'static str> {
    Some(match name {
        "breakline" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "threadline" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "door-leaf" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "door-swing" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "window-sill" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "stair-tread" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "stair-arrow" => "stroke: --stroke-light; stroke-width: 1; fill: none;",
        "align-start" => "align: start;",
        "align-end" => "align: end;",
        "justify-start" => "justify: start;",
        "justify-end" => "justify: end;",
        "sch-line" => "fill: none; stroke: --component-stroke; stroke-width: 1.5;",
        "sch-solid" => "fill: --component-stroke; stroke: none;",
        "sch-tag-line" => "fill: none; stroke: --label-ink; stroke-width: 1.5;",
        "pin-stub" => "fill: none; stroke: --component-stroke; stroke-width: 1.5;",
        "pin-number" => "color: --pin-number; font-size: 10;",
        "ref" => "font-size: 12; font-weight: semibold;",
        "part-value" => "font-size: 12;",
        "net-run" => "width: 40; padding: 0 4;",
        "net-run-turned" => "height: 40; padding: 4 0;",

        "tag-flag-both" => "padding: 2 14;",
        "sheet-caption" => "translate: 10 10; font-scale: 16 15; font-weight: semibold;",
        _ => return None,
    })
}

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

import subprocess, os, sys, itertools
# pairwise error ordering: which error wins when two are present
K = {
    'SHEET': '|page| { sheet: q9; }',
    'TOPIC': '|topic| "x"',
    'UNIT': '|drawing| { unit: furlong; }',
    'POSE': '|schematic| [\n  |R#a| { rotate: 45; }\n]',
    'OP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#b|\n  b.p1 -> b.p2\n]',
    'ENDP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#c|\n  c.p1 - zz\n]',
    'LSHAPE': '|schematic| [\n  |label#l| "x" { shape: zig; }\n]',
    'LSYM': '|schematic| [\n  |label#m| "x" { symbol: zork; }\n]',
    'PSYM': '|R| { symbol: zork; }',
    'TREEDIR': '|box| { layout: tree; direction: up; } [ |topic| "a" ]',
    'TREEROOTS': '|box| { layout: tree; } [\n  |topic| "a"\n  |topic| "b"\n]',
    'SIDE': '|mindmap| "m" [ |topic| "a" { side: top; } ]',
    'ICON': '|icon| "x" { symbol: star; }',
    'LINK': '|link|',
}
names = sys.argv[1:] or list(K)
d = '/tmp/desugar/order2'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
def run(exe, src):
    p = os.path.join(d, 'o.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'desugar', 'o.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    return (r.stdout + r.stderr).decode().strip()
def which(out, la, lb, a, b):
    if not out.startswith('o.lini:'):
        return '?'
    ln = int(out.split(':')[1])
    if ln >= lb:
        return b
    if ln >= la:
        return a
    return '?'
mism = 0
for a, b in itertools.combinations(names, 2):
    res = []
    for x, y in ((a, b), (b, a)):
        sx, sy = K[x], K[y]
        src = sx + '\n' + sy + '\n'
        lx = 1
        ly = sx.count('\n') + 2
        o1 = run('/workspace/executable', src)

import subprocess, os, sys, itertools
# pairwise error ordering: which error wins when two are present
K = {
    'SHEET': '|page| { sheet: q9; }',
    'TOPIC': '|topic| "x"',
    'UNIT': '|drawing| { unit: furlong; }',
    'POSE': '|schematic| [\n  |R#a| { rotate: 45; }\n]',
    'OP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#b|\n  b.p1 -> b.p2\n]',
    'ENDP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#c|\n  c.p1 - zz\n]',
    'LSHAPE': '|schematic| [\n  |label#l| "x" { shape: zig; }\n]',
    'LSYM': '|schematic| [\n  |label#m| "x" { symbol: zork; }\n]',
    'PSYM': '|R| { symbol: zork; }',
    'TREEDIR': '|box| { layout: tree; direction: up; } [ |topic| "a" ]',
    'TREEROOTS': '|box| { layout: tree; } [\n  |topic| "a"\n  |topic| "b"\n]',
    'SIDE': '|mindmap| "m" [ |topic| "a" { side: top; } ]',
    'ICON': '|icon| "x" { symbol: star; }',
    'LINK': '|link|',
}
names = sys.argv[1:] or list(K)
d = '/tmp/desugar/order2'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
def run(exe, src):
    p = os.path.join(d, 'o.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'desugar', 'o.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    return (r.stdout + r.stderr).decode().strip()
def which(out, la, lb, a, b):
    if not out.startswith('o.lini:'):
        return '?'
    ln = int(out.split(':')[1])
    if ln >= lb:
        return b
    if ln >= la:
        return a
    return '?'
mism = 0
for a, b in itertools.combinations(names, 2):
    res = []
    for x, y in ((a, b), (b, a)):
        sx, sy = K[x], K[y]
        src = sx + '\n' + sy + '\n'
        lx = 1
        ly = sx.count('\n') + 2
        o1 = run('/workspace/executable', src)
        o2 = run('/tmp/bin-desugar/executable', src)
        w1 = which(o1, lx, ly, x, y)
        w2 = which(o2, lx, ly, x, y)
        res.append((w1, w2, o1, o2))
    tag = 'same-pass' if res[0][0] != res[1][0] else 'FIXED ' + res[0][0]
    bad = [r for r in res if r[0] != r[1]]
    flag = '' if not bad else '   <-- MINE DIFFERS'
    if bad:
        mism += 1
    print('%-10s %-10s %s%s' % (a, b, tag, flag))
    for r in bad:
        print('      orig:', r[2].splitlines()[0] if r[2] else '')
        print('      mine:', r[3].splitlines()[0] if r[3] else '')
print('mismatches', mism)

import subprocess, os, sys, itertools
# sheet-level errors vs body errors: which wins
S = {
    'DENSITY': '{ density: 0; }',
    'SHADOW': '{ |box::block| { fill: red; } }',
    'CYCLE': '{ |a::b| { fill: red; } |b::a| { fill: red; } }',
    'DEFUNK': '{ |a::zz| { fill: red; } }',
    'SELUNK': '{ |zz| { fill: red; } }',
    'DUP': '{ |a::box| { fill: red; } |a::box| { fill: red; } }',
}
B = {
    'SHEET': '|page| { sheet: q9; }',
    'TOPIC': '|topic| "x"',
    'UNIT': '|drawing| { unit: furlong; }',
    'OP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#b|\n  b.p1 -> b.p2\n]',
    'ENDP': '|schematic| [\n  |R#c|\n  c.p1 - zz\n]',
    'TREEDIR': '|box| { layout: tree; direction: up; } [ |topic| "a" ]',
    'SIDE': '|mindmap| "m" [ |topic| "a" { side: top; } ]',
    'ICON': '|icon| "x" { symbol: star; }',
    'LINK': '|link|',
    'UNKTYPE': '|foo|',
}
d = '/tmp/desugar/order2'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
def run(exe, src):
    p = os.path.join(d, 'o.lini')

    r = subprocess.run([exe, 'desugar', 'o.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    return (r.stdout + r.stderr).decode().strip()
for s, sv in S.items():

        src = sv + '\n' + bv + '\n'

        flag = '' if o1 == o2 else '   <-- MINE DIFFERS'

        if o1 != o2:
            print('      orig:', o1.splitlines()[0] if o1 else '')
            print('      mine:', o2.splitlines()[0] if o2 else '')
for b, bv in B.items():
    src = bv + '\n'
    o1 = run('/workspace/executable', src)
    o2 = run('/tmp/bin-desugar/executable', src)
    flag = '' if o1 == o2 else '   <-- MINE DIFFERS'
    print('alone %-8s %s%s' % (b, o1.splitlines()[0] if o1 else '', flag))
    if o1 != o2:
        print('      mine:', o2.splitlines()[0] if o2 else '')

import subprocess, os, random, difflib, sys
seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
show = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 3
rnd = random.Random(seed)
d = '/tmp/desugar/realsch'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
PARTS = ['R', 'C', 'L', 'D', 'LED', 'F', 'FB', 'Y']
PINS2 = {'D': ['a', 'k'], 'LED': ['a', 'k']}

def gen():
    lines = ['{ layout: schematic; |vcc::label| { symbol: power; } [ "3V3" ] }']
    ics = []
    for i in range(rnd.randint(1, 2)):
        pins = []
        items = []
        for side in ['left', 'right', 'top', 'bottom']:
            for k in range(rnd.choice([0, 1, 2, 3]) if side in ('left', 'right') else rnd.choice([0, 0, 1])):
                name = '%s%d' % (side[0], k)
                items.append('|pin#%s| { side: %s; }' % (name, side))
                pins.append((name, side))
        if len(pins) < 3:
            for k in range(3 - len(pins)):
                name = 'x%d' % k
                items.append('|pin#%s| { side: left; }' % name)
                pins.append((name, 'left'))
        lines.append('|component#u%d| "IC%d" [ %s ]' % (i, i, '; '.join(items)))
        ics.append(('u%d' % i, pins))
    used = set()
    pcount = 0
    for w in range(rnd.randint(1, 6)):
        ic, pins = rnd.choice(ics)
        pin, side = rnd.choice(pins)
        if (ic, pin) in used and rnd.random() < 0.7:
            continue
        used.add((ic, pin))
        chain = ['%s.%s' % (ic, pin)]
        for k in range(rnd.choice([1, 1, 2])):
            t = rnd.choice(PARTS)
            pid = '%s%d' % (t.lower(), pcount)
            pcount += 1
            lines.insert(1 + len(ics), '|%s#%s| "%s"' % (t, pid, rnd.choice(['10k', '100n', '1u', 'BAT54', ''])))
            chain.append(pid)
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.35:
            chain.append('|gnd|')
        elif r < 0.6:
            chain.append('|vcc|')
        elif r < 0.75 and len(ics) > 1:
            other = [x for x in ics if x[0] != ic][0]
            p2, _ = rnd.choice(other[1])
            chain.append('%s.%s' % (other[0], p2))
        lines.append(' - '.join(chain))
    for k in range(rnd.randint(0, 2)):
        ic, pins = rnd.choice(ics)
        pin, side = rnd.choice(pins)
        lines.append('%s.%s %s "%s"' % (ic, pin, rnd.choice(['-', '->', '-<']), rnd.choice(['SDA', 'SCL', 'EN', 'RX'])))
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

ok = 0
fails = []
for i in range(n):
    src = gen()
    p = os.path.join(d, 'g.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'desugar', 'g.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-desugar/executable', 'desugar', 'g.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if (r1.stdout, r1.stderr, r1.returncode) == (r2.stdout, r2.stderr, r2.returncode):
        ok += 1
    else:
        fails.append((src, r1, r2))
print('OK %d / %d  (orig errors among fails: %d)' % (ok, n, sum(1 for f in fails if f[1].returncode != 0)))
for src, r1, r2 in fails[:show]:
    print('=' * 30)
    print(src)
    a = (r1.stdout + r1.stderr).decode().splitlines()
    b = (r2.stdout + r2.stderr).decode().splitlines()
    for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, lineterm='', n=1))[2:40]:
        print(l)

n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
show = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 3
rnd = random.Random(seed)
d = '/tmp/desugar/errfuzz'

ERRS = [
    '|page| { sheet: q9; }',
    '|topic| "x"',

    '|R#rr%d| { rotate: 45; }',
    '|R| { symbol: zork; }',
    '|label#ll%d| "x" { shape: zig; }',

    '|box| { layout: tree; } [\n|topic| "a"\n|topic| "b"\n]',
    '|mindmap| "m" [ |topic| "a" { side: top; } ]',
    '|icon| "x" { symbol: star; }',
    '|link|',
    '|foo|',
    'zz%d - qq',
    'aa%d -> bb',
    '|box| "fine"',
    '|R#ok%d|',
]
def err():
    e = rnd.choice(ERRS)
    if '%d' in e:
        e = e % rnd.randint(0, 99)
    return e

def block(depth):
    out = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.6 or depth > 1:
            out.append(err())
        else:
            c = rnd.choice(['|box| [\n%s\n]', '|schematic| [\n%s\n]', '|drawing| [\n%s\n]', '|group| [\n%s\n]'])
            out.append(c % '\n'.join(block(depth + 1)))
    return out

def gen():
    lines = []
    sheet = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        sheet.append('layout: schematic;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('density: 0;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('unit: furlong;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('.k |zz| { fill: red; }')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('|d::box| [ |topic| "b" ]')
    if sheet:
        lines.append('{\n' + '\n'.join(sheet) + '\n}')
    lines.extend(block(0))
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append('|d|')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

ok = 0
fails = []
for i in range(n):
    src = gen()
    p = os.path.join(d, 'g.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'desugar', 'g.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)

    if (r1.stdout, r1.stderr, r1.returncode) == (r2.stdout, r2.stderr, r2.returncode):

    else:

import subprocess, os, random, difflib, sys
seed = int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv) > 1 else 1
n = int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv) > 2 else 200
show = int(sys.argv[3]) if len(sys.argv) > 3 else 3
rnd = random.Random(seed)
d = '/tmp/desugar/errfuzz'
os.makedirs(d, exist_ok=True)
ERRS = [
    '|page| { sheet: q9; }',
    '|topic| "x"',
    '|drawing| { unit: furlong; }',
    '|R#rr%d| { rotate: 45; }',
    '|R| { symbol: zork; }',
    '|label#ll%d| "x" { shape: zig; }',
    '|box| { layout: tree; direction: up; } [ |topic| "a" ]',
    '|box| { layout: tree; } [\n|topic| "a"\n|topic| "b"\n]',
    '|mindmap| "m" [ |topic| "a" { side: top; } ]',
    '|icon| "x" { symbol: star; }',
    '|link|',
    '|foo|',
    'zz%d - qq',
    'aa%d -> bb',
    '|box| "fine"',
    '|R#ok%d|',
]
def err():
    e = rnd.choice(ERRS)
    if '%d' in e:
        e = e % rnd.randint(0, 99)
    return e

def block(depth):
    out = []
    for _ in range(rnd.randint(1, 3)):
        r = rnd.random()
        if r < 0.6 or depth > 1:
            out.append(err())
        else:
            c = rnd.choice(['|box| [\n%s\n]', '|schematic| [\n%s\n]', '|drawing| [\n%s\n]', '|group| [\n%s\n]'])
            out.append(c % '\n'.join(block(depth + 1)))
    return out

def gen():
    lines = []
    sheet = []
    if rnd.random() < 0.3:
        sheet.append('layout: schematic;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('density: 0;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('unit: furlong;')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('.k |zz| { fill: red; }')
    if rnd.random() < 0.1:
        sheet.append('|d::box| [ |topic| "b" ]')
    if sheet:
        lines.append('{\n' + '\n'.join(sheet) + '\n}')
    lines.extend(block(0))
    if rnd.random() < 0.2:
        lines.append('|d|')
    return '\n'.join(lines) + '\n'

ok = 0
fails = []
for i in range(n):
    src = gen()
    p = os.path.join(d, 'g.lini')
    open(p, 'w').write(src)
    r1 = subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable', 'desugar', 'g.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    r2 = subprocess.run(['/tmp/bin-desugar/executable', 'desugar', 'g.lini'], capture_output=True, cwd=d)
    if (r1.stdout, r1.stderr, r1.returncode) == (r2.stdout, r2.stderr, r2.returncode):
        ok += 1
    else:
        fails.append((src, r1, r2))
print('OK %d / %d' % (ok, n))
for src, r1, r2 in fails[:show]:
    print('=' * 30)
    print(src)
    a = (r1.stdout + r1.stderr).decode().splitlines()
    b = (r2.stdout + r2.stderr).decode().splitlines()
    for l in list(difflib.unified_diff(a, b, lineterm='', n=1))[2:20]:
        print(l)

content.text:
`lini desugar` now matches the original byte-for-byte on the whole corpus: **246/246** (test_doc_examples, blocks, test_samples). The compile comparison is **72/209**, up from the 71 baseline, so nothing regressed, and fmt is still 246/246. Everything is committed on `worktree-agent-a16aa976db9486242` and the working tree is clean.

**Fuzzing on fresh seeds.** Random snippets of each kind were compared against the original:
- **100% match:** general documents, the extended families, drawings, sequences, trees, tables, odd property values, documents containing several errors at once, and realistic schematics (including rotated, mirrored and grid-placed ICs).
- **About 97–98% match:** fully random schematic wirings.
- **CLI wrappers** (stdin, missing file, bad UTF-8, directory, help, extra arguments, `--`) all match.

**What changed this round:**
- **Which error is reported.** When a file has several errors, desugar now reports the same one as the original. The checks run in this order: `|link|` nodes, the define table, tree problems, selectors, then the main lowering, with density and unit errors last. Tree problems are only reported for the document body, never inside define bodies or link labels, which is what the original does.
- **Schematic wiring.**
  - Small components (1–2 pins) now get turned to face their wire.
  - Anything with `cell:` is treated as fixed in place.
  - Branching wires and labels in the middle of a chain are handled.
  - `rotate`, `mirror`, `symbol`, `shape`, `pins`, `side` and `span` now apply when they come from a custom type definition.
  - Define-body wires are routed together with the surrounding schematic.
  - A connector's (`|J|`) pins don't show their names, and pin numbers only appear when the value is a number.
- **Trees and mindmaps.**
  - Directions from mindmaps vs. their containers are handled.
  - `side:` is checked the same way.
  - A mindmap outside a tree is drawn as ordinary boxes.
  - Branch links at the top level are placed in the original's order.
- **Values.**
  - px-per-unit prints the raw product with no rounding (e.g. 95.99929999999999).
  - Page zone counts round halves down.
  - Wall thickness and thread must be a single positive number.
  - Title-block fields and the "did you mean" hints for `sheet:` match.
- **Other.** Sequence-fragment endpoints resolve in the original's order, and floor-plan measurements (`unit-mm`, wall thickness) now also apply inside stacks.

**Edits to shared files** (all small):
- `src/format.rs`: made three internal modules visible to desugar; no behaviour change.
- `src/types.rs`: added missing type entries only (footer, control, shoulder, junction, gnd, nc, opamp, J, and the part types R, C, L, D, LED, Q, Y, F, FB, SW, BT, V, I, M, BZ, TP).
- `src/cli.rs`: the `desugar` subcommand now treats `--` as "end of options" (15 lines, desugar only).

**Known gaps:**
- **Pathological schematics** are the remaining 2–3% of random cases: a part wired back to the same pin, two chains running through one part in opposite directions, pin-to-pin wires on one component, or a label between two fixed-rotation parts. Realistic circuits all match.
- **Loop/alt/opt blocks inside a schematic:** their wires should belong to the surrounding schematic. When there are several errors, this can change which one is reported first.
- **`highlight -- file`** fails the same way `desugar -- file` did. I left it alone because highlight isn't mine.
